smell_validity.evidence: Eight scattered copies in seven plugins each sanitize the template-resolved destination name before it reaches a transport, replacing its direct use, so a naming-rule change forces coordinated edits everywhere with no grep-able pattern. Per-destination rules stay legitimate while the shared mechanism is duplicated, and the driver contract package visibly owns nothing; boundary and cost are unmistakable without the label.

maintenance_impact.evidence: Every policy evolution, a newly forbidden character, a different cap or fallback, requires finding and editing all eight scattered copies; the divergent styles visible in the diff defeat any single search. Future destinations must re-derive naming rules from scratch. Consolidation restores a real long-term ownership boundary in the shared contract package, beyond mere tidying, though scoped to one policy.

development_plausibility.evidence: Each patch sits naturally beside existing template resolution and reads like an incident fix: Chinese comments, protocol-specific limits (255/250), varied idioms echoing the tree's per-plugin habits. The Elasticsearch edit grows around pre-existing inline lowercasing. But one sweep covering every destination writer with maximally varied styles is more complete and systematically irregular than organic incident-by-incident drift would leave.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: The prompt fixes the finished state (one shared, documented mechanism; per-destination rule declarations), the preservation boundary (exact same replaced characters, caps, case, fallbacks, resolution semantics, configurations, wire behavior) and exclusions (row-value and payload resolution stays untouched), and sketches each scattered copy distinctly. This decisively prevents wrong-direction redesign, partial cleanup, and scope creep while leaving implementation open.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Beyond scrubbing, sites need separate decisions for clamping (255/250/none), case (only Elasticsearch), and empty-name fallback (five variants plus absent), each with code-supported differences; character policies are pairwise distinct (whitelist, two replacer tables, byte threshold, regexp, '$', rune set). MongoDB's write and delete paths even resolve from different rows.

localization_burden.evidence: The prompt names every copy's shape and the shared entry point, and all sites resolve through one driver helper, so a single search plus per-file reading finds them. Classifying name versus payload call sites (cache values, message key, MySQL/ClickHouse columns) is local to each plugin; no cross-component combination, aliasing, or registration is needed.

repair_coordination.evidence: Rule choices interlock: char-rule representation constrains how caps and fallbacks compose, emptiness is decided after scrubbing, and MongoDB's write/delete paths resolve different rows, so sites cannot be repaired independently. A partial repair using one row choice succeeds on insert but resolves delete names from the wrong row; dropping the index write-back breaks later commits.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: No uniform rule preserves behavior at even two sites: pairwise-distinct character policies (whitelist, two replacer tables, byte threshold, regexp, '$'-only, rune set), caps at two sites with different limits, lowercase at one, fallbacks in several formats at some sites only. Uniform helper, single replacer, and regexp approaches each fail on input or ordering differences.

behavioral_risk.evidence: Wrong edits compile and pass ordinary events: dropping the memcache clamp surfaces only on >250-byte keys, Elasticsearch without lowercasing only on mixed-case resolved names, wrong row choice only on multi-row batches, missing fallback only on empty resolutions. Multiple special-state paths exist, but the supplied material shows no tests or records confirming any is checked, so 4 is not established.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
